1. `src/services/completions.ts` – `isNativeFunctionMethod`: matching by bare name (`apply`, `call`, `bind`, `length`, `name`, …) with no check that the symbol actually comes from `Function.prototype` (or `CallableFunction`/`NewableFunction`). Any user-defined property/method on a function object that happens to be named `call`, `length`, `name`, etc. (e.g. a custom `.name` or `.length` field, common on decorated/wrapped functions) gets silently deprioritized even though it's exactly the "custom property" case this PR is trying to surface. Fix by resolving the symbol's declaration(s) and checking it's declared on the global `Function` interface (e.g. compare against `typeChecker.getApparentType`/declarations of `lib.es5.d.ts`'s `Function`, similar to how other lib-symbol checks are done elsewhere in this file) rather than name-matching.

2. `src/services/completions.ts` – `isNativeFunctionMethod`: the `type.flags & TypeFlags.Object` check is close to meaningless (unions/intersections of function types, or function types produced via generics, won't necessarily have `TypeFlags.Object` set as a plain flag check) and is redundant with the subsequent call-signature check. Either drop the flag check or replace it with a correct narrowing; as written it both fails to exclude some non-function cases and can reject legitimate function types, reintroducing the bug for arbitrary type shapes.

3. `src/services/completions.ts` – whitespace/formatting: the diff rewrites `addTypeProperties`, `addPropertySymbol`'s surrounding braces, and `isStaticProperty` with no functional change other than line-ending/whitespace churn (every line shows as both removed and added). This bloats the diff and will conflict with `dprint fmt` (the bot's own CI note shows the formatter never actually ran due to the firewall block). Re-run `dprint fmt` / rebase to a clean diff that only touches the lines that actually change.

4. `isNativeFunctionMethod` accepts a `TypeChecker` parameter it never uses. Remove the unused parameter, or if it's meant for future use requiring a legitimate type-based symbol check (see #1), actually use it to resolve `Function.prototype`'s symbol instead of hardcoding the name list.

5. Hardcoded name list omits other `Function.prototype`/`CallableFunction` members such as `[Symbol.hasInstance]`, and anything added via `lib` targets (e.g. nothing today, but the list is version-coupled and will silently rot if lib.d.ts changes). Deriving the set from the actual `Function` interface's members (per #1) avoids this maintenance burden entirely.

6. New test files (`completionBunInspectExample.ts`, `completionFunctionNativeMethods.ts`, `completionFunctionNativeMethodsExtended.ts`) are missing trailing newlines (diff shows "No newline at end of file" for all three) and don't follow this file's established naming/location convention of being generated via the fourslash test harness scripts in most cases — minor but should be fixed before merge: add trailing newlines and run the project's lint/format check on test files.

7. No regression tests for cases where "native-looking" names are legitimately user-defined (the exact gap in #1) — e.g. `interface F { (): void; name: string; }`. Add a test asserting such a custom `name`/`length` property is NOT deprioritized, since that's precisely the scenario the current name-based matching breaks.

8. Scope/missing case: arrow functions and function expressions assigned custom properties outside of an interface (e.g. `const f = () => {}; (f as any).call2 = ...`) and `Function` itself (completing on `Function.prototype` directly, or on `new Function()`) aren't covered — worth at least a comment/test clarifying intended scope, since "any function type" is a broad claim in the PR description but only object-literal-like function types are exercised in tests.
